title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: G is a rank-1 group scheme over a base S, essentially SL2 or GL2 acting on a rank-2 module E, with H possibly a variant such as PGL2 or GL2. sigma is a section with Tr sigma = 0 and det sigma = 1, so sigma^2 = -1 (an element 'of order 4', as in the S-generator of SL2(Z) relevant to the loop equation). T_sigma = Cent_G(sigma) is the centralizer, a torus when sigma is regular semisimple, and N_sigma = Norm_G(T_sigma).

The previous page proves a corollary: for every section eps of mu_2 there exists, fppf-locally, a section tau with [tau, sigma] = eps, i.e. tau(sigma) := tau sigma tau^{-1} = eps sigma.

The page first finishes that argument. Since Tr(eps sigma) = 0 and det(eps sigma) = eps^2 = 1, eps sigma has the same characteristic polynomial as sigma. Since sigma is regular in Steinberg's sense (not a scalar), so is eps sigma. Two regular sections with the same characteristic polynomial are locally conjugate, so tau exists locally.

He then defines (22) N'_sigma = {tau | [tau, sigma] in Gamma mu_2}, a subscheme of G contained in N_sigma by (20). It is right-stable under T_sigma. Better, it is a subgroup scheme: if tau(sigma) = eps sigma and tau'(sigma) = eps' sigma, then tau'tau(sigma) = eps'eps sigma. The map tau -> eps is a homomorphism N'_sigma -> mu_2 with kernel T_sigma. It is fppf-surjective by the corollary, giving the exact sequence (23) 1 -> T_sigma -> N'_sigma -> mu_2 -> 1. This is the familiar 'torus, normalizer, Weyl group of order 2' extension, presented with mu_2 as quotient.

The page ends by starting to compare N' with N. If tau normalizes T_sigma, then tau(sigma) = a sigma + b with a, b in Gamma O_S. The next page takes traces to get 2b = 0. Hence N' = N when 2 is invertible, or more generally when 2 is a non-zero-divisor. In characteristic 2 this can fail, since -nu a^2 + b^2 = -nu need not force b = 0.

All of this prepares the product group B'_0 x A_g x N'_sigma used in the subsequent construction, within the 'variations on the loop equation' part of the Longue Marche.
errors: The inclusion N'_sigma subset N_sigma is asserted in the definition before being justified. It does follow from (19)-(20) on the previous page, so this is a gap of presentation only.

Surjectivity of N'_sigma -> mu_2 holds only fppf-locally, by the corollary. In characteristic 2, sigma with Tr sigma = 0 and det sigma = 1 satisfies sigma^2 = 1 and is unipotent, so T_sigma is not a torus there. Grothendieck tacitly restricts the torus picture; the next page notes the characteristic-2 discrepancy between N' and N.
Minor: the 'conditions numériques' plus regularity give local conjugacy of sigma and eps sigma (Steinberg / SGA3-type result for regular elements). This is invoked rather than proved.

ideas.what: Local conjugacy of regular elements with the same characteristic polynomial (regular in Steinberg's sense = non-scalar for GL2), over a general base
ideas.modern_name: Steinberg's theorem on regular elements; Chevalley/Kostant section, relative version
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steinberg (1965); relative versions in SGA3 and later work
ideas.where_published: SGA3 treats regular elements and Cartan subgroups; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Subgroup N'_sigma = {tau : [tau, sigma] in mu_2} and exact sequence 1 -> T_sigma -> N'_sigma -> mu_2 -> 1; equality with the normalizer of the torus when 2 is a non-zero-divisor
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer of a (nonsplit) maximal torus in SL2 and its Weyl group extension
ideas.where_published: SGA3 (normalizers of maximal tori, Weyl group schemes) in general form

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-scheme computation: the normalizer of the centralizer torus of a trace-zero element of SL2, with a mu_2 quotient. It is careful about characteristic 2, but nothing here is new beyond being a technical step in the unpublished loop-equation notes.
transcription_corrections: Last lines: 'si tau in Gamma G normalise T_sigma' (not 'Gamma sigma').
'le sous-schéma de N_sigma' is crossed out and replaced by 'G (ou de H)'.
'tau'sigma = eps'sigma' should read tau'(sigma) = eps' sigma.
